subject: Ω-INVERSE-PROBLEM-T∞
definition: General OAK-safe inverse-problem kernel that analyzes rank, nullity and conditioning before routing to Moore-Penrose, Tikhonov, nonlinear local or linear-Gaussian Bayesian reconstruction.

claims.text: For small linear systems, the implementation computes a bounded reference Moore-Penrose representative and reports rank/nullity/conditioning plus forward residuals.
claims.scope: small dense matrices in the stdlib-only Jacobi/small-Gram reference kernel
assumptions: numerical rank tolerance is appropriate to scaling
the forward matrix is the intended model
modes below the Gram finite-precision resolution floor are treated as numerical null modes
failure_conditions: NumPy pinv baseline materially disagrees on declared reference families
rank/nullity is unstable under reasonable tolerance changes
a null-space ambiguity is presented as unique recovery

claims.text: The implementation provides a damped finite-difference Gauss-Newton inverse step with residual-decreasing backtracking for local nonlinear reconstruction.
claims.scope: small smooth nonlinear maps near a usable initial guess
assumptions: the selected branch is reachable from the initial guess
failure_conditions: local convergence is presented as a global uniqueness theorem

claims.text: For a declared linear-Gaussian model, the implementation computes the closed-form posterior mean and covariance.
claims.scope: finite-dimensional nonsingular prior and noise covariance matrices
assumptions: Gaussian prior and likelihood are the intended model
failure_conditions: posterior result is presented as prior-independent evidence
covariance inputs are singular but treated as invertible

metadata.families: square, tall, wide, deterministic random, rank-deficient

m_minus.observation: The first implementation formed A^T A for every matrix geometry. Independent NumPy comparison exposed false inversion of numerical null modes for wide matrices.
m_minus.correction: Use the smaller Gram matrix A^T A or A A^T according to shape and enforce a sqrt(machine-epsilon) singular-value resolution floor.
m_minus.lesson: An exact algebraic identity can still be a poor finite-precision algorithm.

risks: numerical rank sensitivity to scaling and threshold
local nonlinear solver converging to the wrong branch
next_actions: Pass final exact-head dedicated CI including NumPy baseline court.
Add tolerance/scaling campaigns against production SVD baselines.
Add null-space basis and resolution-matrix diagnostics.
Add constraints, generalized Tikhonov and robust losses.
Add nonlinear Bayesian and multimodal branch representations.

metadata.oak_boundary: Executable prototype candidate; no large-scale numerical superiority, global identifiability, or physical uniqueness claim.
